_comment: The MCP servers Claude Code sees on this machine, applied at user scope by `agent-sync mcp sync` on every ralph up. Each entry mirrors `claude mcp add --scope user <name> -- <command> [args...]`: a stdio entry has `command` and optional `args` and `env`; a remote one has `transport` (http or sse), `url` and optional `headers`. A leading ~ in command and args is expanded. `hosts` and `profiles` gate an entry to those hostnames (lowercased) or ralph profile tags (from ~/.config/ralph/config.local.toml); both gates must pass. Names starting with _ are skipped. Drop-ins (~/.config/claude-mcp/servers.d/*.json) merge over this file by name. A server missing from `claude mcp list` is added; one whose registered spec differs is removed and added again; a remote server is compared by url alone, so an OAuth login survives. A server dropped from here stays registered unless mcp.prune is true in config.yaml.

csl._comment: Code search. Pure stdio over the local index; nothing has to be running.

humanizer._comment: Sandboxed: the wrapper ships with the thismoon humanizer recipe in the ralph sources cache. It pulls only the judge backend vars from the secrets file, scrubs env with env -i, cd-s to / and execs humanizer mcp through srt-run with ~/.config/srt/humanizer.json, which recipes/humanizer here provides.

kof._comment: A thin client of the kof service: registered everywhere, the tools answer unreachable until `kof serve` runs.

deps._comment: Profile-gated: the deps service runs on personal machines only (the override example in config.toml), so the server registers only where the personal profile is set.

speak._comment: Host-gated: speak plays audio through this machine's speakers and its TTS engine lives on one host. The name is the machine's hostname as `hostname` prints it, lowercased.

present-shared._comment: A remote server, compared by url alone so a login done by hand survives a sync. Secrets never go in this file: an OAuth flow or a headersHelper command mints the header at launch.
